units.title: Hello, letters and getting by in class
units.goal: Greets, thanks, apologises, gets attention and asks for repetition with fixed chunks; spells their name; follows classroom instructions
units.rationale: Grammar-free entry: real exchanges are possible from day one with memorised chunks, and the alphabet and tu/vous choice underpin everything that follows

units.title: The sounds and spelling of French
units.goal: Hears and produces the oral and nasal vowels and key consonants, reads accents, links sounds to common spellings and knows which final letters are silent
units.rationale: French spelling is far from its pronunciation; an early, explicit sound–spelling pass prevents fossilised reading errors in every later unit

units.title: Who I am: être, avoir and introductions
units.goal: Introduces themselves and others (name, nationality, country) with être, avoir, subject and tonic pronouns and c'est
units.rationale: The two most frequent verbs and the pronoun system are needed for almost every sentence; introductions give them an immediate use

units.title: Numbers, personal details and family
units.goal: Gives and understands numbers, dates of birth, addresses and phone numbers; talks about their family; asks yes/no questions; fills in a form
units.rationale: Personal information is the first real transaction (forms, registration); the 70–99 system needs dedicated practice

units.title: Things around me: gender, articles, il y a, negation
units.goal: Names everyday objects with the right gender and article, says what there is and is not
units.rationale: Gender and the article system are the backbone of the noun phrase; il y a and ne … pas allow first descriptions

units.title: Describing people and things
units.goal: Describes appearance, character, clothes and objects with agreeing adjectives, possessives and demonstratives
units.rationale: Agreement and adjective position build on gender and articles; description is a core A1 function

units.title: Daily routine and time
units.goal: Tells the time, gives dates and describes a daily routine with present-tense regular, irregular and reflexive verbs
units.rationale: The present-tense paradigms are introduced through the routine, where they are used repeatedly and naturally

units.title: Asking questions; weather and news
units.goal: Asks for information with question words and quel, talks about the weather and asks after people
units.rationale: Information questions need the present tense; this unit turns learners from responders into askers

units.title: Likes, leisure and invitations
units.goal: Talks about likes and leisure, invites, accepts and refuses, and congratulates with modal verbs and basic connectors
units.rationale: Modals (pouvoir, vouloir, devoir) unlock invitations and refusals; connectors start linking sentences

units.title: Food and shopping
units.goal: Buys food and goods, asks prices and quantities, and orders in a café or restaurant politely
units.rationale: The partitive and quantities are needed for the most common travel transaction; je voudrais is taught as a polite chunk

units.title: Places, directions and transport
units.goal: Locates places, asks for and follows directions, uses transport and describes their town
units.rationale: Place prepositions and the imperative are needed together for directions

units.title: Plans and the near future
units.goal: Talks about plans and holidays with aller + infinitive, recent past with venir de, necessity and purpose
units.rationale: The near future is formed with a known verb (aller) and gives a first time reference beyond the present

units.title: What I did: the passé composé
units.goal: Says what they did yesterday or last weekend with the passé composé and time indicators; describes a past moment with c'était
units.rationale: The first past tense comes after the present paradigms and the participle forms it reuses

units.title: Home, work and appointments
units.goal: Describes their home and job, makes appointments, and uses on and ça as in everyday speech
units.rationale: Consolidates A1 grammar in two key life domains and introduces the very frequent on

units.title: Reading and writing everyday texts
units.goal: Reads personal messages, public notices and tourist information; understands announcements; writes short messages and gives a short prepared talk
units.rationale: Integrates A1 into the text types and activities listed by the Inventaire, with reading/listening strategies and writing conventions

units.title: Telling a story in the past
units.goal: Narrates a sequence of past events with être/avoir agreement and chronological connectors; talks about work experience
units.rationale: Extends the A1 passé composé to connected narration, the central A2 function

units.title: Description in the past: the imparfait
units.goal: Describes past situations and habits with the imparfait and combines it with the passé composé; tells a short biography
units.rationale: The imparfait is only meaningful against the passé composé, so it follows narration directly

units.title: Future, conditions and wishes
units.goal: Talks about future events with the futur simple, real conditions with si + present, and wishes and intentions
units.rationale: The futur simple builds on infinitives and the conditional chunks already known

units.title: Object pronouns, y and en
units.goal: Replaces objects and places with le/la/les, lui/leur, y and en in the present and passé composé
units.rationale: Pronoun placement is a major French difficulty; it needs the verb constructions from A1

units.title: Pronouns and relative clauses
units.goal: Uses possessive, demonstrative and indefinite pronouns and links clauses with qui, que and où
units.rationale: Relatives and pronouns let learners build longer descriptions and definitions

units.title: Comparing and evaluating
units.goal: Compares people, places and products; says what they liked and disliked; uses exclamations and tout
units.rationale: Comparison and evaluation are needed before opinions and choices

units.title: Opinions, agreement and reasons
units.goal: Agrees and disagrees, gives and asks for opinions, justifies them with reasons and consequences, expresses reservations
units.rationale: Builds on comparison and connectors to support simple argument

units.title: Going out and organising together
units.goal: Makes and reacts to suggestions, organises a joint activity and offers help
units.rationale: Social planning recycles modals, the conditional chunk and on in a cooperative task

units.title: Health, advice and obligation
units.goal: Describes symptoms and physical states, gives advice and warnings, and expresses obligation and prohibition
units.rationale: Health is a key A2 survival domain and the natural context for advice and obligation

units.title: The telephone and managing conversation
units.goal: Makes phone calls, opens and closes conversations, interrupts politely, checks understanding, paraphrases and asks for details
units.rationale: Interaction management is listed as key discourse content at A2; phone calls make it necessary without visual support

units.title: Places, customs and feelings
units.goal: Presents a country or town, its customs and environment, and expresses feelings
units.rationale: Moves from describing one's surroundings to describing a culture and personal reactions

units.title: Services, problems and notices
units.goal: Complains and asks for solutions, follows instructions and rules, handles money conventions, reads nominalised notices
units.rationale: Service encounters with problems are a typical A2 need for travellers and residents

units.title: Grammar consolidation: negation, prepositions, time
units.goal: Uses ne … plus / rien / personne, verbs and adjectives with à/de, sans + infinitive, frequency adverbs and time expressions
units.rationale: Gathers the remaining A2 grammar points that refine sentences already being produced

units.title: Study, presentations and media
units.goal: Talks about education, gives a short presentation, reads the press and follows simple media
units.rationale: Integrates A2 into the reception text types the Inventaire lists for the press and broadcast media

units.title: Writing and mediation
units.goal: Writes formal emails, blog posts and messages to shops, and relays simple information between languages
units.rationale: Written production and mediation need explicit tasks that the Inventaire does not itemise

units.title: Strategies and varieties of French
units.goal: Guesses words from context, scans texts, recognises regional varieties and spoken features
units.rationale: Strategies and variety awareness prepare learners for unadapted input beyond the course
